Two more plugins, absorbed from the coredhcp/plugins repository and rewritten.

## Added

- netbox: serves each client the address NetBox documents on the interface
  that carries its MAC, on devices and virtual machines alike (NetBox 4.2 or
  newer). DHCPv4 gets the address and the subnet mask from the prefix
  length, DHCPv6 an IA_NA with a configurable lifetime. Answers sit in a
  bounded LRU with separate TTLs for hits and misses, so a boot storm costs
  one pair of API calls per client. Tokens as `env:NAME` or literal; v2
  (`nbt_`) tokens go out as Bearer, legacy ones as Token
- redis: static leases, router, DNS servers and lease time from a Redis hash
  per MAC, for both families. `host:port` or `redis://` / `rediss://` URLs
  with credentials and database; `password:env:NAME`. The protocol is spoken
  directly over a small RESP2 client in the standard library, so the module
  gains no dependency
- `make test-redis`: the redis plugin's integration tests against a real
  Redis in compose, also run in CI

Both plugins pass unknown clients on to the next plugin, as file does, and
drop the request when the backend fails, so a client with a documented
address is never handed a pool address because its backend hiccuped.

## Changed

- 99.1% statement coverage, both new packages at 100%

## Container image

Multi-arch (linux/amd64, linux/arm64):

    docker run --rm ghcr.io/hyperized/coredhcp:0.2.0 -P
    docker run --rm --net host \
        -v /etc/coredhcp:/etc/coredhcp:ro \
        ghcr.io/hyperized/coredhcp:0.2.0

The entrypoint reads /etc/coredhcp/config.yaml; the server needs the host
network to share a broadcast domain with its clients.
